correctness.rationale: Exact orthonormal affine kernel and convex-order monotonicity for zero-mean two-point laws prove maximality of the rare corner for every n and every 0<p_i<1; independent summation preserves convex order. Row sign functions attain norms, negative kernel mass attains the [0,1] defect. Fair parity identities and homogeneous binomial tails follow from exact counting, fixed-bias and rare-bias asymptotics from CLT/Poisson convergence with bounded normalized second moments. The embedded checker independently passed 54049 exact tests; finite checks do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: A claim-level comparison against published published-finding corpus records, recorded related scientific claims and four primary full-text sources found no result implying the arbitrary heterogeneous Bernoulli rare-corner extremal kernel, exact L∞ norm, all-bias monotonicity and sharp positivity defect. Known L2 ANOVA, biased FKN and infinite Lp/Hardy projection results supply the framework but not this quantitative classification. The elementary fair-binomial identity is not claimed novel. The main residual risk is an equivalent endpoint formula hidden in the broader Hoeffding-projection literature.
residual_risks: A general prior theorem on L∞ endpoint norms of first-order Hoeffding projections under atomic product measures could imply the result without matching titles or keywords.

value.rationale: The object is the canonical first-order ANOVA approximation on independent heterogeneous binary experiments. Its L2 optimality does not control pointwise instability or negativity. An exact attained all-bias L∞ norm and positivity defect, a convex-order fairness monotonicity principle, and natural fixed-bias/rare-event limiting regimes determine the robustness of this ubiquitous approximation without ad hoc parameter slices. The result is structural and computationally reproducible, not merely a known binomial sum.
